objective: The home page's right column shows a small Recent games list: the latest completed games in the database, best-ranked matchups first.
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: FRONTEND-036, FRONTEND-038 and FRONTEND-039 have merged to main. Test-first: commit the failing tests alone before the implementation; the implementation commit edits no test.

GET /events/games/recent?limit= is public, like the other /events reads. limit is 1 to 10, default 5; anything else is a 422. It is declared before /events/games/{game_id}, so 'recent' is never parsed as an id, and a test pins that.

Candidates are the completed games (Game.completed) on the three most recent distinct dates that have one, of any game_type. 'Recent' means the latest in the database, never relative to today, so a database last loaded two weeks ago still answers with its newest games.

Each candidate team's rank is its league-wide position, 1 to 30, in the regular-season standings of the candidate's own season, using standings' existing order (exact win percentage, then wins, then name) across both conferences. A team with no regular-season game that season ranks after every team that has one.
Candidates are ordered by home_rank + away_rank ascending, so two top teams come first and two bottom teams last; ties go to the newer date, then the higher game id. The first limit are returned.
Each item carries id, date, game_type, label, home_team and away_team (TeamRefOut), home_score, away_score, home_rank and away_rank. An empty database answers 200 with an empty list.

The read is a fixed number of statements whatever limit or the candidate count, pinned by a statement-counting test, and reuses events.service's record aggregation rather than a second standings query. If the dates step needs an index that does not exist, the unit adds it in a migration and states the query plan in the PR.

In the rail's slot from FRONTEND-036, a section headed 'Recent games' (h2) lists the items in the order given. Each row shows both TeamIcons, the abbreviations and GameScore, and links to /games/<id> carrying the modal flow's state, so the game opens over the home page. The row's accessible name reads both teams and the score.

The section reads once per visit to / with a staleTime of 5 minutes, and only while the rail is mounted. Loading is the shared Skeleton rows at the final height, so the landing list moves nothing; a failure shows InlineAlert with Retry; an empty list hides the section entirely.
No horizontal overflow in the rail at the rail's breakpoint (FRONTEND-039's R), 1280 and 1920 CSS px with a classic 17px scrollbar, with the longest team abbreviations and three-digit scores.

Browser rows at R, 1280 and 1920, light and dark, on the dev database with the stats fixture loaded, reported with measurements or NOT DONE: the list and its order checked against /stats standings; a row opening the game over home; keyboard; 200% text size at 1280; the empty database.
frontend/src/test/bundle-budgets/EVENTS-013.ts declares, in the test commit, every output the unit changes. Entry growth is at most 2 KiB raw and 1 KiB gzip, and no output reaches 500,000 raw bytes.
No new dependency, third-party request, image file, or raw colour or px font size in module CSS.
wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x02-events.md records the route and its ordering, and 0x08-frontend.md the section.
